status_summary: S.4615, the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, was reported by the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and placed on the Senate calendar on 2026-05-20, with a written report filed on 2026-08-05; its Sec. 601(c) would make the Director of the Office of Intelligence and Counterintelligence a presidential appointee confirmed by the Senate, reporting directly to the Secretary, for a six-year term and with substantial intelligence community expertise, effective 2029-01-21. The House FY2027 intelligence authorization bill, H.R.9624, was introduced on 2026-07-09 and ordered reported on 2026-07-20, and its introduced text contains no such provision. A CRS report of 2024-06-07 describes the director under existing statute as reporting directly to the Secretary and appointed by the Secretary with Director of National Intelligence concurrence, and DOE's office page lists an acting director as of 2026-10-18.

timeline.event: The Senate Select Committee on Intelligence reported S.4615, the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, as an original measure and it was placed on the Senate calendar (Calendar No. 420); Sec. 601(c) would make the DOE intelligence director a Senate-confirmed presidential appointee with intelligence community expertise reporting to the Secretary, effective 2029-01-21.
The Senate Select Committee on Intelligence filed its written report on S.4615 (S. Rept. 119-133).
